metadata.name: North Dakota Aeronautics Commission Project Prioritization
metadata.source_citation: ACRP Synthesis 123 (2023), Chapter 4 — State of North Dakota case example, pp. 37-39. Sourced from interview with Kyle Wanner, Executive Director, NDAC, April 28, 2022. NDAC's process is explicitly described as 'both objective and subjective, which the state director believes is critical.'

decisions_log.author: APH m49 Sprint 6 reference encoder
decisions_log.decision: Encoded North Dakota as dual_objective_subjective weighting_model — the canonical ACRP example for this pattern.
decisions_log.rationale: NDAC explicitly bifurcates: (1) objective merit ranking of safety/preservation/federal-leverage projects; (2) subjective override allowing NDAC to fund lower-objective-ranked projects with high economic impact, justified to commissioners. Encoded all 11 ACRP-list factors in the objective layer with discretion_override_allowed=true in the tradeoff_layer.
decisions_log.source: ACRP Synthesis 123 p. 37 — 'NDAC's process is both objective and subjective, which the state director believes is critical'

decisions_log.author: APH m49 Sprint 6 reference encoder
decisions_log.decision: Used the 11 ACRP-list factors verbatim per ACRP Syn 123 p. 38 'NDAC is one of the states that uses all 11 factors listed in the survey.'
decisions_log.rationale: ACRP explicitly lists ND's 11 factors: Regulatory mandate; Safety; Security; Level of customer service or capacity; Airport size; Revenue generation/cost reduction; Environmental/community; Sustainable development; Asset preservation; Contribution to goals; Risk factors.

criteria.label: Regulatory Mandate / Compliance
criteria.description: Project addresses regulatory mandate or compliance directive.

subcategories.label: Mandated by statute or FAA directive

criteria.label: Safety
criteria.description: Safety is a high priority per NDAC. Safety issues at runway/RSA, obstructions, and approach surfaces score highest.

criteria.label: Security
criteria.description: Security is one of NDAC's 11 factors.

criteria.label: Customer Service / Capacity
criteria.description: Improves level of service or addresses capacity.

criteria.label: Revenue Generation / Cost Reduction
criteria.description: NDAC requires a business plan for state/local-only revenue-producing projects (hangars, fuel systems). These are LOWER priority in the objective layer but may be elevated in subjective layer if economic impact justifies it.

subcategories.label: Strong revenue / cost benefit with business plan

criteria.label: Environmental / Community
criteria.description: Environmental or community benefits and impacts.

criteria.label: Sustainable Development Initiative
criteria.description: Project advances a sustainable development goal.

criteria.label: Asset Preservation
criteria.description: System preservation (maintaining existing pavement) is a HIGH priority per NDAC. New pavement is a LOWER priority.

criteria.label: Contribution to Goals and Objectives
criteria.description: Project advances NDAC strategic goals or NDASP goals.

subcategories.label: Advances a North Dakota Airport System Plan goal

criteria.label: Risk Factors
criteria.description: Environmental, financial, schedule, or operational risk if project not done.

criteria.label: Federal Funding Leverage (Bonus)
criteria.description: Per NDAC: 'Leveraging federal funding ranks high. If they get a federal grant, it automatically gets high priority for a match.'

governance.statute_citation: ND state aeronautics law sets the standard for annual review but does not govern how grants are issued — described in ACRP Syn 123 as 'general and vague so it can be flexible.'
governance.approval_process: Objective layer ranks projects by merit. Subjective layer allows NDAC to fund lower-ranked projects when justified (e.g., large economic impact). NDAC recommends a list, opens it for public comment, then commissioners vote. Process is intentionally flexible.

disclaimer: Encoding mirrors ACRP Synthesis 123 (2023) summary of NDAC's 11-criterion dual objective/subjective process. ACRP does not publish NDAC's exact per-criterion point allocations; point values are inferred from documented relative priorities (safety high; preservation high; federal leverage high; revenue-producing low at the objective layer, with subjective layer recovering them). Verify against NDAC's internal scoring matrix before adoption.
